name: Arabic gum
aliases: E414, gum arabic, Arabic gum, acacia gum, gum acacia, Acacia senegal gum, Acacia seyal gum, goma arábiga, gomme arabique
what_is: A dried plant exudate, mainly from Acacia or Senegalia species, composed largely of complex polysaccharides and used as an emulsifier, stabiliser, carrier and thickener.
why_botia: Arabic gum is a natural exudate from acacia trees and dissolves in water with very little thickening, which is why it is used in soft drinks and sweets. The small intestine does not digest it: it reaches the colon and ferments there, which makes it a fibre — in fact, it is sold as a fibre supplement. In high amounts it can cause gas, and JECFA did not see a need to set a limit.
can_1: Identify E414, gum arabic, Arabic gum or acacia gum when declared on the label.
can_2: Trigger the E-number and texture information layers.
cannot_1: Determine the amount used when it is not quantified on the label.
cannot_2: Determine the exact Acacia or Senegalia source species or processing grade from the generic ingredient name.
